verdicts.evidence: lines 619-629: sendBtn and sigBtn both have listeners that change state and re-render; 'Start again' resets to draft; queued state is a deliberate inert state with reason shown. Links at 353-359, 371-372, 520-521, 566, 580-581 point to /signup, /login or ids that exist.

lines 385-394, 444-446, 481-485: sample invoice records (INV-0140 to INV-0142, Example Contractor Ltd, 1,200.00, 450.00, 20% CIS, 1,410.00) are hardcoded and visible. The brief did not ask for sample data; the label that it is made up sits inside the page (405, 479).
Single page with no step that depends on an earlier step or screen.
No text inputs or multi-step task; the only inputs are one demo checkbox (458) and two demo buttons (400-401).

line 458: the only preselected value is the demo reminders checkbox, checked, which changes only the illustration (CSS 257-262). Demo starts in draft with nothing sent (595-596). No dialogs, no Enter default.

lines 359, 371, 520, 566: starting a trial is one click to /signup from the sticky header, the hero, the price card and the closing section; sign in is one click (358). The brief places signup at /signup.

Sections map to brief facts: hero and steps (367-427) on-site invoicing, features 436-502 offline, reminders, CIS/VAT, exports, pricing 506-524, FAQ 526-560, footer 571-585 company and support. No testimonials, stats or unrelated sections. Repetition is judged under COPY-004.

Header 358-359: plain 'Sign in' link plus one btn-primary. Hero 371-372: one btn-primary plus a text link. Demo card 400-401: one filled button and one ghost (CSS 168-172). Price card 520 and closing 566 have one primary each.
No action deletes, overwrites or is irreversible; the demo buttons only change an on-page illustration (619-629).

lines 608-610, 615: in the queued state the send button is aria-disabled, relabelled 'Waiting for signal', and the status line directly above (398) reads 'Saved on your phone. It will send as soon as you are back online.'
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in the file.

line 405: 'An illustration with made-up figures, not a screenshot.'; line 479: 'Illustration: made-up figures'; lines 442, 457: 'Illustration: ...'. Visible text tells the visitor the data is mocked and how the page was made.

line 374: 'No card needed to start. Then 12 pounds per user per month. Cancel any time.' sits directly under the trial button it informs. The illustration labels (405, 479) are counted under COPY-001. No other callouts, banners or warnings.
No sentence narrates the page layout. The only usage hints are 'Try it.' (405) and 'try the switch' (457), each one short line at the control it concerns.

lines 493 vs 497-499: tiles 'Export to Xero / QuickBooks / Sage' restate the adjacent paragraph. 510 vs 515-516: intro restates the 30 days and no card ticks beside it. FAQ answers 532-552 repeat 374, 425, 439, 454, 476, 493 almost word for word.

line 412: heading 'Job done, invoice gone.' is a slogan; line 433: 'Built for how trades firms actually work.' is stock promotional wording naming nothing concrete; line 509: 'One price. Nothing to work out.' No exclamation marks or greetings.

Labels: 'Start free trial'/'Try free' (359), 'Start your free 30 days' (371, 520, 566), 'Send invoice' (400, 613), 'Get back in signal'/'Lose signal' (602), 'Start again' (607), 'Sign in' (358). 'Waiting for signal' (610) is the inert in-progress label.

No field names, enum values or developer terms. Terms are trade terms: 'CIS deduction', 'Reverse charge: customer accounts for VAT' (392-393), 'Amount due', 'Waiting for signal' (444). data-state values are attributes only, never shown.
Static page with no requests and no error path; the script (588-631) has no failure branch.
Static page that cannot show an error or warning.
All lists and tables are fixed markup (387-396, 443-447); none can have zero items.
No filters, search or loading; no view can be empty.
Fully static page; no fetch, XHR or form post in the script (588-631).
Every action is a synchronous re-render (598-617); nothing can take a second.
No asynchronous data, so no loading or empty state.
All displayed values are fixed text in the markup; nothing varies in length or count.
No edits that are saved by an explicit action.
No form fields with format constraints; the only input is a demo checkbox (458).
No form with required and optional fields.
No form and no validation.
No form that can reject input.
No form that can be rejected.
No form that can reject input.
No form element or submit button; signup happens at /signup (359, 371).
Nothing is sent to a server; the demo send button only changes local state (619-624).

lines 619-629: each click handler calls render() synchronously, which changes the status text, button labels and data attributes (598-617). Checkbox toggle changes switch, timeline and message through CSS (245-262).

lines 605-616: after Send, the status line states 'Saved on your phone. It will send as soon as you are back online.' or 'Sent to Example Contractor Ltd...'; signal change updates 'Online'/'No signal' (601). Toggle shows On/Off text (467-468).

line 606: the 'Sent to Example Contractor Ltd...' status is the only sign that the invoice went; nothing else on the demo shows the sent result. It is an inline status, not a toast over a visible result.
No error states and no transient messages; the status line (398) persists until the next action and there are no timers in the script.
No action removes, archives or moves anything real; demo controls only change an illustration.
No irreversible action; the demo 'Send invoice' sends nothing (619-624) and offers 'Start again' (607).
No confirmation dialogs; no confirm() or dialog element in the file.
No background requests, so no optimistic updates.
No modal dialogs.
No modal dialogs.

lines 364-375: the first block in main is the hero with the largest type on the page (h1 clamp up to 4.5rem, CSS 114-117), the product statement and the trial button; steps, features, price and FAQ follow below at smaller sizes.
lines 367-374: the opening states what the product is, who it is for and the next step. Hero is sized by padding and content (CSS 105-108), with no min-height or viewport-height rule.

lines 510-513: the only summary figures are the price (12 pounds per user per month) and the worked example of 60 pounds for five, both informing the decision to start a trial. No stat cards or charts.
No view can be filtered, searched or sorted.

All controls are native: links, two button elements (400-401), a real checkbox kept focusable with a focus ring on its label (CSS 234, 247), and details/summary (530-557). Skip link at 344. aria-disabled keeps the send button focusable. No focus traps.

Signal state has text 'No signal'/'Online' (382, 601); pills carry text (444-446); red deduction rows carry a minus sign and label (393, 484); switch shows position plus 'On:'/'Off:' text (467-468); demo status colour change comes with text (605-612).

line 398: the demo status paragraph has role="status" in the initial markup and is filled by textContent (616). line 466: the reminder message container has aria-live="polite" in the markup. sigBtn exposes aria-pressed (603).
lines 530-557: all FAQ items use native details/summary. No other accordions, menus or tabs; the signal button is a toggle with aria-pressed (401, 603), not a disclosure.

CSS 92-96 shortens the header button under 420px; 121 makes the hero button full width; 105, 187, 201, 283 stack to one column; timeline and table sized in fr/100%. Section nav hides under 860px (83-86) but all sections are reached by scrolling and the hero link (372).
Single-screen product; the header nav (352-357) holds only in-page anchors.
One view with no tabs, filters, pagination or selected record; section anchors already use URL fragments (353-356).
Single-view page.
Links onward to /signup and /login in the header (358-359), hero (371), price card (520-521), closing (566) and footer (580-581); brand link returns to top (348). No dead-end states.
No dialogs or overlays.
No stepped flow; the numbered 'steps' list (414-427) is descriptive content, not a task sequence.

CSS 57 btn min-height 48px, 66 btn-big 56px, 67 btn-small 44px, 80 brand 44px, 89 signin min-height 44px, 169 demo buttons 46px, 238 toggle label 52px, 309 summary 56px, 330 footer links padded 10px on 15px text at 1.6 line height.

CSS 70-76: the only sticky element is the header at 64px min-height, under a tenth of a 667px viewport, at the top so it covers no end content. Line 339 sets scroll-margin-top 80px so anchored sections clear it.

lines 367-369: eyebrow 'Invoicing for building and trades firms', h1 'Send the invoice before you leave site.', lede 'Write it on your phone, from a quote or from scratch, and send it by email or text...'. A reader can say what it is and who uses it.

lines 367-371 with CSS 76, 105-123: at 1280 wide, header 64 + padding 72 + eyebrow, 4-line h1 at 72px, lede and button end near 700px; at 375 wide, header 64 + padding 40 + h1 at 40px, lede and full-width button end near 560-600px. Demo is below on phones.

Illustrations at 377-406, 441-448, 456-470, 478-487 depict product behaviour (offline queue, reminder schedule, CIS sums), not stock decoration, but the UI is invented and the queue (443-447) and export tiles (496-500) add nothing the text lacks. Two readings disagreed.

Price 12 pounds per user per month, 30 days free, no card, cancel any time (374, 513-518, 536, 565) match the brief; 60 pounds for five (510) is arithmetic on it. No testimonials, logos, ratings or usage figures. Sample invoice figures are judged under TASK-002.
line 513: '12 pounds' with 'per user, per month' and line 517 'Billed monthly' are visible in the price card with no interaction; also stated in the hero note (374).
No img, picture or video elements; the only graphics are a small inline SVG mark (349) and CSS-drawn illustrations.
No announcement or promotional strip.
No commands or code for the reader to use.

Two accent hues. Yellow --hivis: primary buttons (62), h1 highlight (118), step numbers (194), timeline dots (253). Green --green: eyebrow (111), focus ring (41), tick marks (297), FAQ plus sign (314), switch (245), signal bars (141). Red (21) also used for deductions.
